description: We are interested in coding and finding innovative solutions to fix modern problem
summary: TerraSense is a website that lets blind and low-vision users explore NASA Earth Information Center visualizations by sound, keyboard and screen reader. Users choose a frame and move across it to hear tones generated live in the browser: the app reads the color under the pointer, matches it to the frame’s legend, and turns the approximate value into pitch. It includes, Summary, jump, compare and Where am I features, plus spoken replies to every action, give the sound meaning without needing a mouse. Terrasense does this by having an AI assistant called "Terra" that would help Blind users navigate the website through voice commands such as "Where am I" or "tell me the temperature of the gulf of alaska" or "Let me see the precipitation data please", and it would also brief the blind users on how the website work so they can use it effectively. This addresses the challenge by utilizing live NASA data and pairing it with an accessible website that could help blind students independently explore data without requiring outside assistance, an aspect that is rare on many science websites as it also solves a major painpoint for Blind students, and educators.
details:
What it does: TerraSense Jukebox turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into sound. Users move across a frame by keyboard, mouse or touch. The app reads the color at that spot, matches it to the frame’s legend to get an approximate value, and plays a live tone, higher for higher values. Summary, jump, compare and Where am I tools, plus it allows the user to ask questions and have a real conversation of the data through Terra.

Benefits, extended impact: Blind and low-vision students can explore real NASA data independently instead of relying on someone to describe a picture. It is free, runs in a browser and can work offline. Even though this is currently a prototype, I have spoken to the Bangkok School for the blind's head principal, and they stated that a major issue was that a lot of the learning material were inaccessible, so this project was made to bridge the gap, and give them equal learning opportunities. Moreover, I will also pitch this project in addition to my other project to the school to spread awareness, and give them a learning tool that their students can reliable use.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, Canvas API, ARIA live regions, browser speech, NASA frames and legends, the website was assisted by Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 3.8 flash on AntiGravity IDE.
